environment.description: Same Flask application deployed behind an nginx reverse proxy (v1.25.3) with a location block that adds headers to all proxied responses. The nginx configuration includes: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'" always; and add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always; applied via the server block's location / directive. Note: the 'always' parameter ensures headers are added even on error responses. The CSP script-src 'none' directive prevents ALL script execution regardless of origin, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff prevents MIME-type sniffing. However, the SVG file itself is still served with Content-Type: image/svg+xml and the file content is not sanitized - the control relies entirely on browser-side enforcement of the CSP header to prevent script execution within the SVG context.

config.infrastructure: EC2 t3.medium behind nginx 1.25.3 reverse proxy
config.nginx_config_snippet: location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080; add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'" always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always; }
config.note: CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are injected at the reverse proxy layer, not in application code. The application itself has no awareness of these headers.
